Every phenomenon this deposit touches, and the rule for the rest — 4 machine-checked theorems of the ℤ/9 vortex deposit, one Lean namespace, wing the floor. 4 close by exhaustion over a finite domain (by decide). Every one is sealed live in the append-only ledger.

How these theorems are bound. "Entangled" is used in this deposit's honest sense: correlation by derivation, not quantum entanglement, and no information travels through it.

1 · Shared definitions. 2 definition(s) are used by two or more theorems, binding 12 pair(s); the theorems fall into 1 strand(s), the largest of 4. Most binding: entries (4), statusOf (4).

2 · Imports. Built on: no other cluster. Built on it: no other cluster. Checking this cluster needs 1 file(s): src/proof/phenomena.lean.

3 · The joint address. The 4 sealed receipts fold to 7c2c40c6-89f6-8eb8-bc77-10aca5a1c56f. Order-invariant: yes — the same root in reverse order. Altering one receipt changes it: yes, computed on this run. A content-address proves integrity, not truth.

4 · The address lattice. Each theorem sits at the seven ray values its page plots from its receipt, taken mod 9: a point of (ℤ/9)⁷. This cluster's centre is (7, 5, 2, 8, 4, 2, 0). Its nearest clusters, ranked by lift — pairs observed among each theorem's seven nearest points, over the pairs expected by chance from the two clusters' sizes: families.lean (4 observed, 1.86 expected, lift 2.15), elementary.lean (3 observed, 1.42 expected, lift 2.11), mechanical.lean (6 observed, 4.75 expected, lift 1.26). A lift near 1 is what chance gives. Mean distance between two of its theorems: 16.33; from one of its theorems to a theorem of another cluster: 15.6. A receipt is a hash, so nearness on this lattice is a property of the addresses, not of the mathematics; the mathematical binding is (1) and (2). Chance, measured: over 200 reshufflings of which cluster each point belongs to (seeded, so every rebuild gives the same numbers), a best lift at least this high arose in 56.0% of them — consistent with chance.

Prior art. the SI base quantities and their defining constants are definitions of the Conférence Générale des Poids et Mesures (2019 revision, effective 20 May 2019); the electrochemical results are Michael Faraday's laws of electrolysis, 1834, and the standard enthalpy of combustion of hydrogen. Every physical result named here has an earlier author or a standards body, and none is this deposit's. Per-theorem prior-art searches — OEIS, zbMATH Open, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv — are recorded, with what was searched, where and when, in the living ledger src/proof/novelty.json. No novelty is claimed here.
